title: HYROX Owns Inaction; BAPS Sidesteps the Harm
description: The public apologies of the week, scored.
intro: HYROX leads by accepting responsibility for failing to intervene, though checkable changes remain missing. BAPS lands last for apologising for possible inconvenience without addressing female staff being sidelined.

items.headline: HYROX apologises for failing to stop Beijing competitor after soiling
items.summary: HYROX faced hygiene concerns after allowing a competitor who soiled herself to finish its Beijing race. Co-founder Moritz Fürste acknowledged that organisers should have intervened, accepted responsibility and apologised to those affected while promising immediate rule changes.
items.verdict: Fürste accepts responsibility for not intervening, but the evidence gives no checkable rule changes.

items.headline: BAPS apologises for Eiffel Tower controversy without acknowledging exclusion of women
items.summary: BAPS issued an apology after reports that female Eiffel Tower staff were sidelined during its delegation’s visit prompted a strike. Its statement said the visit was coordinated with management, denied knowledge of anyone being denied access, and apologised to anyone hurt or inconvenienced without addressing the treatment of female staff.
items.quote: Nevertheless, we sincerely apologise to anyone who may have been hurt or inconvenienced by this situation
items.verdict: Apologises for possible inconvenience but never addresses female staff being sidelined or offers repair.

items.headline: Steve Ballmer apologizes to Clippers fans, accepts NBA sanctions
items.summary: After the NBA sanctioned the Clippers for salary-cap circumvention, Steve Ballmer apologized to fans, employees and fellow owners for the resulting distress and distraction. He said the team had paid its $30 million fine and would comply with the penalties, while maintaining disagreements with the investigation’s findings.
items.quote: I want to apologize to our fans, employees, and my fellow NBA team owners for the distraction and distress this matter has caused
items.verdict: Pays the $30 million fine but apologizes for distraction, not salary-cap circumvention.

items.headline: Trey Parker and Matt Stone Apologize for Kendrick Lamar Film Delay
items.summary: Trey Parker and Matt Stone publicly accepted responsibility for delaying Whitney Springs, their film collaboration with Kendrick Lamar. They apologized to pgLang and Paramount, cited South Park commitments and personal circumstances, and expressed continued belief in the project without offering a new deadline or remedy.
items.quote: We take full responsibility for the schedule delay of this movie.
items.verdict: Accepts responsibility for delaying Whitney Springs but offers no remedy or revised release date.

items.headline: Rodri apologises over Valencia remarks but says comments were taken out of context
items.summary: Rodri publicly apologised after television footage reportedly showed him calling Valencia weak during Barcelona’s win. He said he had also called Valencia captain Jose Gaya to apologise to the squad, but described his remarks as surprise rather than mockery.
items.quote: First and foremost, I’d like to apologise to anyone who may have felt offended,
items.verdict: Apologises to Valencia but avoids repeating his criticism and blames missing context.

items.headline: Optus apologises after outage disrupts emergency calls
items.summary: A 76-minute Optus outage on September 11 disrupted voice services, including some emergency calls. Optus apologised to customers, said services had been restored and reported referring 41 calls to Victoria Police for welfare checks.
items.quote: We sincerely apologise to customers for the disruption.
items.verdict: Optus names calling failures and reports restoration and welfare referrals, but offers no prevention commitment.

items.headline: France regrets post questioning US commitment to human rights
items.summary: France’s UN mission expressed regret for a July X post questioning Washington’s commitment to human rights after a UN vote. The statement narrowed the disagreement to that vote and reaffirmed the alliance, following US moves to block France’s next ambassador.
items.quote: regrets the message published on July 25, 2026 on X, which questioned the US commitment to human rights
items.verdict: Identifies the human-rights post and expresses regret, but offers no repair or prevention steps.
